mechanism_narrative: The continued rise in WORKPLACES mobility signals strengthening weekday activity and foot traffic that spills into nearby retail and dining trips, so RETAIL_REC should increase over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days after four consecutive weeks of improving WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while TRANSIT stays deeply depressed, more trips are absorbed locally rather than shifted to central-city shopping, which keeps RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -70 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT staying below -70 and RESIDENTIAL staying above +15.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week improvement in PARKS mobility indicates warmer or more permissive outdoor activity, and that same leisure recovery typically precedes broader retail visitation, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after PARKS increases by at least 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues to recover from extreme suppression, access friction to shopping districts falls and retail trips rebound over the following month; the effect is strongest when WORKPLACES are also moving upward.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -72 after being below -73
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days after TRANSIT crosses above -72.

mechanism_narrative: A gradual decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals people spending more time away from home, which is consistent with more discretionary out-of-home spending and a higher RETAIL_REC level over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days as RESIDENTIAL keeps falling or stays below the current level.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps converging toward baseline while RETAIL_REC remains depressed, household errand traffic is normalizing without a matching leisure-shopping rebound, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above -2 while RETAIL_REC remains below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays above -2 and RETAIL_REC remains below -35 at the trigger point.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained weekly improvement in TRANSIT reflects widening travel access, and that expanded accessibility should feed into higher retail visitation with a one-week lag rather than an immediate effect.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after TRANSIT improves for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, flat or falling WORKPLACES mobility suppresses discretionary trips by keeping commuting and lunch-time spillovers weak, so retail-and-recreation stays below the recent four-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean over the next month while WORKPLACES does not recover from its current level.
